force after applying for the relevant licenses as required by the regulatory framework, as well as the production, industrialization, processing, commercialization, conditioning, transportation and stockpiling of grains and products derived from
grains, as well as any other activity complementary to its industrial and commercial business or any activity which may be necessary to attain its objective. In order to fulfill these objectives, the Company may set up, become associated with or
have an interest in any public or private entity domiciled in Argentina or abroad, within the limits set forth in the Bylaws. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Filing with the

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of June&nbsp;30, 2024, the Group carries out its operations in accordance with the following structure: </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The operations, properties and clients of the Group are mainly located in Argentina. However, the Group also holds participating interest in exploratory

<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>2.a) Applicable accounting framework </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The condensed interim
consolidated financial statements of the Company for the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT> period ended June&nbsp;30, 2024 are presented in accordance with IAS 34 &#147;Interim Financial Reporting&#148;. Therefore, they should be
read together with the annual consolidated financial statements of the Company as of December&nbsp;31, 2023 (&#147;annual consolidated financial statements&#148;) presented in U.S. dollars and in accordance with IFRS as issued by the IASB. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">These condensed interim consolidated financial statements corresponding to the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT> period ended
June&nbsp;30, 2024 are unaudited. The Company believes they include all necessary adjustments to reasonably present the results of each period on a basis consistent with the audited annual consolidated financial statements. Net Income for the <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT> period ended June&nbsp;30, 2024 does not necessarily reflect the proportion of the Group&#146;s full-year net income. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>2.b) Material accounting policies </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The material accounting
policies are described in Note 2.b) to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The accounting policies adopted in the preparation of these
condensed interim consolidated financial statements are consistent with those used in the preparation of the annual consolidated financial statements, except for the valuation policy for income tax detailed in Note 18. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Functional currency </U></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As mentioned in Note
2.b.1) to the annual consolidated financial statements, YPF has defined the U.S. dollar as its functional currency. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The consolidated financial
statements used by YPF for statutory, legal and regulatory purposes in Argentina are those in pesos and filed with the CNV and approved by the Board of Directors and authorized to be issued on August&nbsp;8, 2024. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Share-based benefit plans </U></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Group maintains
share-based benefit plans with the characteristics mentioned in Note 37 of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements and Note 37 to the annual consolidated financial statements. Such plans are recorded in accordance with the
guidelines set out in IFRS 2 &#147;Share-based Payments&#148;. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="2%">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">-</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify">Equity-settled share-based payment transactions are recognized as a straight-line expense over the period of service
based on the Group&#146;s estimate of the number of equity instruments that will eventually vest considering their fair value at the grant date, with an offsetting credit entry in the &#147;Share-based benefit plans&#148; account in the statement of
changes in shareholders&#146; equity. At the end of each period, the Group reviews its estimate according to the number of equity instruments it expects will vest based on the grant conditions specified under the respective benefit plan.

<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Adoption of new standards and interpretations effective as from January</U><U></U><U>&nbsp;1, 2024</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Company has adopted all new and revised standards and interpretations, issued by the IASB, relevant to its operations which are of mandatory and
effective application as of June&nbsp;30, 2024, as described in Note 2.b.14) to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Standards and
interpretations issued by the IASB as of January</U><U></U><U>&nbsp;1, 2024 whose application is not mandatory at the closing date of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements and have not been adopted by the Group</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In accordance with Article 1, Chapter III, Title IV of the CNV Rules, the early application of the IFRS and/or their amendments is not permitted for
issuers filing financial statements with the CNV, unless specifically admitted by such agency. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="justify" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt"><B>IFRS 18 &#147;Presentation and disclosure in financial statements&#148; </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In April 2024, the IASB issued IFRS 18, which replaces IAS 1 &#147;Presentation of financial statements&#148;, with the objective of providing better
information on the financial performance of entities, improving their comparability, which is applicable to fiscal years beginning on or after January&nbsp;1, 2027. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">IFRS 18 introduces the following information requirements that can be grouped into 2 main groups: </P>
<P STYLE="font-size:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="2%">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">-</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify">Group income and expenses into 3 defined categories: (i)&nbsp;operating; (ii) financing and (iii)&nbsp;investing, and
include certain defined subtotals, such as the operating result and the result before financing and income tax, with the aim of improving the comparability of the statement of comprehensive income. </P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="2%">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">-</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify">Provide more information about the performance measures defined by management, which, although not mandatory, in the
event of including this type of measures, the entity must disclose the reason why said measures are useful to financial statements users, their method of calculation, a reconciliation between to the most directly comparable subtotal from the
statement of comprehensive income, among others. </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Additionally, IFRS 18 establishes more detailed guidance on how to organize
information within the financial statements and whether it should be provided in the primary financial statements or in the notes, with the aim of improving the grouping of information in the financial statements. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of the date of issuance of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements, the Group is in the process of evaluating the effects of the
application of IFRS 18. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="justify" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt"><B>IFRS 19 &#147;Subsidiaries without public accountability: Disclosures&#148; </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In May 2024, the IASB issued IFRS 19 with the objective of allowing the option to apply simplified disclosure requirements in the financial statements of
subsidiaries without public accountability and with a parent company, ultimate or intermediate, that prepares consolidated financial statements for public use in accordance with IFRS. Its application is optional for fiscal years beginning on or
after January&nbsp;1, 2027. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:70pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="font-size:70pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:7pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="right">HORACIO DANIEL MAR&Iacute;N </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:7pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="right">President&#8195;&#8195;&#8195;&#8195;&#8195; </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>2.c) Significant estimates and key sources of estimation uncertainty </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In preparing the financial statements at a certain date, the Group is required to make estimates and assessments affecting the amount of assets and
liabilities recorded and the contingent assets and liabilities disclosed at such date, as well as income and expenses recognized in the period. Actual future profit or loss might differ from the estimates and assessments made at the date of
preparation of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The assumptions relating to the future and other sources of uncertainty
about the estimates made for the preparation of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements are consistent with those used by the Group in the preparation of the annual consolidated financial statements, which are disclosed in Note
2.c) to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>2.d) Comparative information </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Amounts and other information corresponding to the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2023 are an integral part of these condensed interim consolidated
financial statements and are intended to be read only in relation to these financial statements. Amounts corresponding to the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT> period ended June&nbsp;30, 2023 presented in these financial statements
for comparison purposes correspond to the functional currency of the company according to IAS&nbsp;21 (see Note 2.b)). </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Additionally, from this fiscal
year, the Group has made a change in the presentation of the items in the &#147;Financial results, net&#148; line item in the statement of comprehensive income (see Note 29). This change is intended to provide more relevant and detailed information
on the origin of financial results and the effects of transactions or conditions that affect the financial situation, financial performance, and cash flows of the Group such as interests and exchange differences generated by loans, among others; and
improve the comparability of the Group&#146;s financial statements with its peers. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:10pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<TD WIDTH="2%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><B><A NAME="item1toc854147_9"></A>3.</B></TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify"><B>SEASONALITY OF OPERATIONS </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Historically, the Group&#146;s results have been subject to seasonal fluctuations throughout the year, particularly as a result of the increase in natural
gas sales during the winter driven by the increased demand in the residential segment. Consequently, the Group is subject to seasonal fluctuations in its sales volumes and prices, with higher sales of natural gas during the winter at higher prices.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B><A NAME="item1toc854147_10"></A>4. ACQUISITIONS AND DISPOSALS </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Dissolution of the company YPF International </U></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On
May&nbsp;6, 2024, the Plurinational Service of Registry of Commerce (&#147;SEPREC&#148; by its acronym in Spanish) of Bolivia approved the dissolution and liquidation of YPF International. </P>

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify"><B>FINANCIAL RISK MANAGEMENT </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Group&#146;s activities expose it to a variety of financial risks: Market risk (including exchange rate risk, interest rate risk, and price risk),
credit risk and liquidity risk. Within the Group, risk management functions are conducted in relation to financial risks associated to financial instruments to which the Group is exposed during a certain period or as of a specific date. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">During the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT> period ended June&nbsp;30, 2024, there were no significant changes in the administration or
policies of risk management implemented by the Group as described in Note 4 to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">

<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="justify" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt"><B>Liquidity risk management </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Most of the Group&#146;s loans contain market-standard covenants for contracts of this nature, which include financial covenants in respect of the
Group&#146;s leverage ratio and debt service coverage ratio, and events of defaults triggered by materially adverse judgements, among others. See Notes 16, 32 and 33 to the annual consolidated financial statements and Notes 17 and 33. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Group monitors compliance with covenants on a quaterly basis. As of June&nbsp;30, 2024, the Group is in compliace with its covenants. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">It should be noted that, under the terms and conditions of the loans that our subsidiary Metrogas has taken, the interest coverage ratio would not have
been complied with, which could have accelerated the maturities of these financial liabilities. However, the financial creditors formally accepted to waive Metrogas from complying with the contractual obligation related to such financial ratio, as
of June&nbsp;30, 2024. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify"><B>BUSINESS SEGMENT INFORMATION </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The different business segments in which the Group&#146;s organization is structured consider the different activities from which the Group can obtain
revenues and incur expenses. Such organizational structure is based on the way in which the chief decision maker analyzes the main operating and financial magnitudes for making decisions about resource allocation and performance assessment, also
considering the business strategy of the Group. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Business segment information is presented consistently with the manner of reporting the information
used by the chief decision maker to allocate resources and assess business segment performance. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The business segment structure is organized as
follows: </P> <P STYLE="font-size:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="justify" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt"><B>Upstream </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Upstream business segment performs all activities related to the exploration and exploitation and production of crude oil, natural gas
and frac sand for well drilling/fracking purposes. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Its revenues are largely derived from: (i)&nbsp;the sale of the crude oil produced
to the Downstream business segment; and (ii)&nbsp;the sale of the natural gas produced and the natural gas retained in plant to the Gas and Power business segment. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">It incurs all costs related to the activities mentioned above. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="justify" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt"><B>Downstream </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Downstream business segment performs activities related to: (i)&nbsp;crude oil refining and the production of petrochemical products;
(ii)&nbsp;logistics related to the transportation of crude oil to the refineries and the transportation and distribution of refined and petrochemical products to be marketed at the different sales channels; (iii)&nbsp;commercialization of refined
and petrochemical products obtained from such processes; (iv)&nbsp;commercialization of crude oil; and (v)&nbsp;commercialization of specialties for the agribusiness industry and of grains and their
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">by-products.</FONT> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Its revenues are derived primarily from the sale of crude oil, refined and
petrochemical products, specialties for the agribusiness industry and grains and their <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">by-products.</FONT> These operations are performed through the businesses of B2C (Retail), B2B (Industries, Transportation,
Aviation, Agro, Lubricants and Specialties), LPG, Chemicals, International Trade and Transportation and Sales to Companies. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:70pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="justify" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt"><B>Gas and Power </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Gas and Power business segment performs activities related to: (i)&nbsp;natural gas transportation to third parties and the Downstream
business segment and its commercialization; (ii)&nbsp;commercial and technical operation of the LNG regasification terminal in Escobar by hiring regasification vessels; (iii)&nbsp;transportation, conditioning and processing of natural gas retained
in plant for the separation and fractionation of natural gasoline, propane and butane; (iv)&nbsp;distribution of natural gas through our subsidiary Metrogas; and (v)&nbsp;the storage of the natural gas produced. Also, through our investments in
associates and joint ventures, the Gas and Power business segment undertakes activities related to: (i)&nbsp;separation of natural gas liquids and their fractionation, storage and transportation for the production of ethane, propane, butane and
natural gasoline; (ii)&nbsp;generation of conventional thermal electric power and renewable energy; and (iii)&nbsp;production, storage, distribution and sale of fertilizers. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Its revenues are largely derived from the commercialization of natural gas as producers to third parties and the Downstream business
segment, the distribution of natural gas through our subsidiary Metrogas, the sale of natural gasoline, propane and butane to the Downstream business segment and the provision of LNG regasification services. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">It incurs all costs related to the activities mentioned above, including the purchase of natural gas and natural gas retained in plant
from the Upstream business segment. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">This segment covers other activities performed by the Group not falling under the business segments mentioned above and which are not

<TD WIDTH="2%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><B>9.</B></TD>

<p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Group capitalizes the financial cost of loans as part of the cost of the property, plant and
equipment. For the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT> periods ended June&nbsp;30, 2024 and 2023, the rate of capitalization was 7.66% and 8.13%, respectively, and the amount capitalized amounted to 4 and 10, respectively. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B><A NAME="item1toc854147_24"></A>18. INCOME TAX </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">According to IAS 34, income tax expense is recognized in each interim period based on the best estimate of the effective income tax rate expected as of
the closing date of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements, considering the tax criteria that the Group assumes to apply during the fiscal year. If the estimate of such rate is modified based on new elements of judgment, the
income tax expense could require adjustments in subsequent periods. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In relation to such tax criteria, the income tax expense contemplates the
application of the integral inflation adjustment mechanism applicable to property, plant and equipment, and the indexation of the accumulated tax losses carryforward until the concurrence of the projected tax result of the fiscal year 2024, all
considering that the assumption of confiscation would be verified in accordance with the jurisprudence of the CSJN in force as of the date of issuance of these consolidated financial statements. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Company considers having strong arguments to successfully defend such assumed tax criteria, in the event of a possible controversy with the tax
authorities, in accordance with the guidelines of IFRIC 23 &#147;Uncertainty over income tax treatments&#148;. As of June&nbsp;30, 2024, the assumed tax criteria generates a profit of 336. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The income tax charge for the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT> period ending June&nbsp;30, 2024 is a profit of 200. The amount accrued
for the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-periods</FONT> ending June&nbsp;30, 2024 and 2023 is as follows: </P> <P STYLE="font-size:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B><A NAME="item1toc854147_37"></A>31. SHAREHOLDERS&#146; EQUITY </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of June&nbsp;30, 2024, the Company&#146;s capital amounts to 3,919 and treasury shares amount to 14 represented by 393,312,793 book-entry shares of
common stock and divided into four classes of shares (A, B, C and D), with a par value of 10 pesos and 1 vote per share. These shares are fully subscribed, <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">paid-in</FONT> and authorized for stock exchange listing.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of June&nbsp;30, 2024, there are 3,764 Class&nbsp;A outstanding shares. As long as any Class&nbsp;A share remains outstanding, the affirmative
vote of the Argentine Government is required for: (i)&nbsp;mergers; (ii) acquisitions of more than 50% of YPF shares in an agreed or hostile bid; (iii)&nbsp;transfers of all the YPF&#146;s production and exploration rights; (iv)&nbsp;the voluntary
dissolution of YPF; (v)&nbsp;change of corporate and/or tax address outside Argentina; or (vi)&nbsp;make an acquisition that would result in the purchaser holding 15% or more of the Company&#146;s capital stock, or 20% or more of the outstanding
Class&nbsp;D shares. Items (iii)&nbsp;and (iv) also require prior approval by the Argentine Congress. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On April&nbsp;26, 2024, the General
Shareholders&#146; Meeting was held, which approved the statutory financial statements of YPF (see Note 2.b)) corresponding to the year ended on December&nbsp;31, 2023 and, additionally, approved the following in relation to the retained earnings:
(i)&nbsp;completely disaffect the reserve for future dividends, the reserve for purchase of treasury shares and the reserve for investments; (ii)&nbsp;absorb accumulated losses in unappropriated retained earnings and losses up to the amount of
1,003,419&nbsp;million of pesos (US$ 1,244 million); (iii) allocate the amount of 28,745&nbsp;million of pesos (US$ 36 million) to constitute a reserve for purchase of treasury shares; and (iv)&nbsp;allocate the amount of 3,418,972&nbsp;million of
pesos (US$ 4,236 million) to constitute a reserve for investments. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">During the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT> periods ended
June&nbsp;30, 2024 and 2023, the Company has not repurchased any of its own shares. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B><A NAME="item1toc854147_38"></A>32. EARNINGS PER SHARE </B></P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>33. CONTINGENT ASSETS AND LIABILITIES (cont.) </B></P> <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>33.b.2) Contentious claims </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Contentious claims are described in Note 33.b.2) to the annual consolidated financial statements. Updates for the
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT> period ended June&nbsp;30, 2024, are described below: </P> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="justify" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt"><B>Petersen Energ&iacute;a Inversora, S.A.U. and Petersen Energ&iacute;a, S.A.U. (collectively, &#147;Petersen&#148;) -
Eton Park Capital Management, L.P., Eton Park Master Fund, LTD. and Eton Park Fund, L.P. (collectively, &#147;Eton Park&#148;, and together with Petersen, the &#147;Plaintiffs&#148;) </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The appeals filed by the parties in these proceedings (see Note 33 to the annual consolidated financial statements) will be fully briefed by
September&nbsp;6, 2024. After the briefing is completed, the Second Circuit Court of Appeals will set a date for oral argument. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On April&nbsp;1,
2024, Plaintiffs filed a turnover motion, which became public (and accessible to YPF) on April&nbsp;22, 2024. This motion requests that the District Court order the Republic to turn over the YPF Class&nbsp;D shares held by the Republic to Plaintiffs
in partial satisfaction of the District Court&#146;s judgment against the Republic in this proceeding. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Plaintiffs and the Republic completed their
briefing on the turnover motion on July&nbsp;8, 2024. The District Court may, but is not required to, hold oral argument prior to rendering a decision on the turnover motion. Furthermore, the District Court&#146;s decision on the turnover motion may
be appealed by Plaintiffs or the Republic in accordance with applicable procedural rules. YPF is not a party to the turnover motion. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Plaintiffs are
also seeking discovery of documents from YPF related to their theory that YPF could be an &#147;alter ego&#148; of the Republic. YPF denies that it is an <I>alter ego</I> and objected to Plaintiffs&#146; document requests. On May&nbsp;28, 2024, the
District Court ordered YPF to produce documents in response to Plaintiffs&#146; discovery requests. To date, Plaintiffs have not requested that the District Court find that YPF is an <I>alter ego</I> of the Republic, and the District Court&#146;s
order on discovery is not a ruling accepting Plaintiffs&#146; <I>alter ego</I> theory. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">YPF will continue to defend itself in accordance with the
applicable legal procedures and available defenses. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Company will continue to reassess the status of the litigation and its possible impact on the
results and financial situation of the Group, as needed. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B><A NAME="item1toc854147_40"></A>34. CONTRACTUAL COMMITMENTS </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>34.a) Exploitation concessions, transport concessions and exploration permits </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The most relevant agreements, exploitation concessions, transport concessions and exploration permits that took place in the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2023 are described in Note 34.a) to the annual consolidated financial statements. During the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT> period ended June&nbsp;30, 2024, there were no significant updates. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>34.b) Investment agreements and commitments and assignments </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The most relevant investment agreements and commitments and assignments are described in Note 34.b) to the annual consolidated financial statements.
During the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT> period ended June&nbsp;30, 2024, there were no significant transactions. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B><A NAME="item1toc854147_41"></A>35. MAIN REGULATIONS </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>35.a) Regulations applicable to the hydrocarbon industry </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Updates to the regulatory framework described in Note 35.a) to the annual consolidated financial statements for the
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT> period ended June&nbsp;30, 2024, are described below: </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>35.a.1) Hydrocarbons Law </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Through the Bases Law (see Note 35.j)), amendments were incorporated in relation to the Hydrocarbons Law, as described below: </P>
<P STYLE="font-size:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="2%">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">-</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify">Establishes that international trade of hydrocarbons will be free, according to the terms and conditions established by
the PEN. </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="2%">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">-</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify">Establishes that exploration permit holders and/or exploitation concessionaires, refiners and/or marketers may freely
export hydrocarbons and/or their derivatives, subject to the SE&#146;s <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-objection.</FONT> The effective exercise of this right will be subject to regulations issued by the PEN, which, among other aspects, must
consider: (i)&nbsp;the usual requirements related to the access to technically proven resources; and (ii)&nbsp;that the eventual objection of the SE may only be formulated within 30 days of being informed of the exports to be made, and must be based
on technical or economic reasons related to the security of supply. </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="2%">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">-</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify">Incorporates hydrocarbon processing and natural gas storage activities, for which the national or provincial Executive
Branch, as the case may be, may grant storage and/or processing authorizations. </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="2%">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">-</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify">Changes the legal figure of &#147;transport concession&#148; to the figure of &#147;transport authorization&#148;.
</P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="2%">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">-</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify">Establishes that exploitation concessions and transportation concessions granted prior to the enactment of the Base Law
will continue to be governed until their expiration by the legal framework existing at the date of approval of the Bases Law. </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="2%">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">-</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify">Determines that in exploitation concession bidding processes the royalties to be paid to the application authority will
be offered by the concessionaire, determining that the royalty to be offered will be 15% plus or minus a percentage to be chosen by the bidder. </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="2%">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">-</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify">Other modifications establish that: (i)&nbsp;the request for conversion of a conventional exploitation concession into
a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-conventional</FONT> exploitation concession will only be available until December&nbsp;31, 2028 and its term will be 35 years without extensions; (ii)&nbsp;for new&nbsp;exploitation concessions, the national or
provincial Executive Branch, as applicable, at the time of defining the terms and conditions of the bidding, may determine in a reasoned manner other terms of up to 10 years more than those provided for in the Hydrocarbons Law; (iii)&nbsp;owners of
projects and/or facilities for the conditioning, separation, fractionation, liquefaction and/or any other hydrocarbon industrialization process may request an authorization to transport hydrocarbons and/or their derivatives to their
industrialization facilities and from the same to subsequent industrialization or commercialization process centers and/or facilities; (iv)&nbsp;those authorized to process hydrocarbons must process hydrocarbons from third parties up to a maximum of
5% of the capacity of their facilities; and (v)&nbsp;the fee for each square kilometer or fraction thereof that a holder of an exploration permit must pay annually and in advance shall be calculated according to a scale determined by the price of a
barrel of oil quoted on the &#147;Frontline ICE Brent&#148;. </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>35.b) Regulations applicable to the Downstream segment </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">During the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT> period ended June&nbsp;30, 2024, there were no significant updates to the regulatory
framework described in Note&nbsp;35.b) to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="font-size:150pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<P STYLE="font-size:12pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:7pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="right">HORACIO DANIEL MAR&Iacute;N </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>35. MAIN REGULATIONS (cont.) </B></P> <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>35.c) Regulations applicable to the Gas and Power segment </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Updates to the regulatory framework described in Note 35.c) to the annual consolidated financial statements for the
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT> period ended June&nbsp;30, 2024, are described below: </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>35.c.1) Transportation, distribution and
commercialization of natural gas </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Through the Bases Law (see Note 35.j)), amendments were incorporated in relation to the Gas Law, as described
below: </P> <P STYLE="font-size:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="2%">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">-</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify">The PEN is entrusted with regulating natural gas exports following the same terms and conditions as for liquid
hydrocarbon exports as described in Note 35.a.1). </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="2%">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">-</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify">Establishes a special regime for long-term firm export authorizations for liquefied natural gas. </P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify">Incorporates the figure of &#147;underground natural gas storage authorizations in depleted natural hydrocarbon
reservoirs&#148;. </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify">Contemplates the possibility for the providers of public natural gas distribution and transportation services to
request the renewal of their licenses for an additional <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">20-year</FONT> period. </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify">Creates the &#147;Ente Nacional Regulador del Gas y la Electricidad&#148;, which will replace and assume the functions
of the &#147;Ente Nacional Regulador de la Electricidad&#148; (&#147;ENRE&#148;) and ENARGAS. </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>35.c.2) Regulatory requirements applicable to
natural gas distribution </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Tariff schemes and tariff renegotiations </U></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On April&nbsp;3, 2024, ENARGAS Resolution No.&nbsp;120/2024 was published in the BO, approving the transition tariff tables and rates and charges for
services to be applied by Metrogas as from such date, and the tariff update formula applicable on such transition tariff tables as from May 2024. On May&nbsp;27, 2024, the tariff updates corresponding to May, June and July 2024 were postponed by
instruction of the SE to ENARGAS, which generated an objection by Metrogas to such instructions. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On June&nbsp;6, 2024, ENARGAS Resolution
No.&nbsp;260/2024 was published in the BO, approving the transition tariff tables and rates and charges for services to be applied by Metrogas as from such date. See Note 35.d). </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">These transition measures will remain in force until the rates resulting from the RTI come into force, in accordance with the provisions of
Decree&nbsp;No.&nbsp;55/2023. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>35.d) Incentive programs for hydrocarbon production </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Updates to the regulatory framework described in Note 35.d) to the annual consolidated financial statements for the
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT> period ended June&nbsp;30, 2024, are described below: </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Plan for Reinsurance and Promotion of
Federal Hydrocarbon Production Domestic Self-Sufficiency, Exports, Imports Substitution and the Expansion of the Transportation System for all Hydrocarbon Basins in the Country 2023-2028 (&#147;Plan GasAr 2023-2028&#148;) </U></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On March&nbsp;27, 2024, SE Resolution No.&nbsp;41/2024 was published in the BO, which approved natural gas prices at the PIST in U.S. dollars
corresponding to the awarded volumes entered into within the framework of the Plan GasAr 2023-2028 which will be applicable for natural gas consumptions made: (i)&nbsp;from April&nbsp;1 and until April&nbsp;30, 2024; (ii) from May&nbsp;1 and until
September&nbsp;30, 2024; and (iii)&nbsp;from October&nbsp;1 and until December&nbsp;31, 2024; and instructed that, for the purpose of transferring the prices of natural gas to the tariff schemes of the public service of distribution of natural gas,
ENARGAS issue the tariff schemes that reflect on a monthly basis the variation of the exchange rate of the prices of natural gas to be transferred to the tariff schemes. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>35. MAIN REGULATIONS (cont.) </B></P> <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On 5&nbsp;June 2024, SE Resolution No.&nbsp;93/2024 was published in the BO, which approved natural gas
prices at the PIST in U.S. dollars corresponding to the awarded volumes entered into within the framework of the Plan GasAr 2023-2028 which will be applicable for natural gas consumptions from June 2024 and leaves without effect the instruction to
ENARGAS to issue tariff schemes that reflect on a monthly basis the variation of the exchange rate of the prices of natural gas to be transferred to the tariff schemes. See Note 35.c.2). </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>35.e) Investment incentive programs </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Large Investment
Incentive Regime (&#147;RIGI&#148;) </U></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Bases Law (see Note 35.j)) created the RIGI, intended to encourage large investments with tax, customs
and exchange benefits, guaranteeing legal&nbsp;certainty and the protection of acquired rights. This regime seeks to encourage investments, promote economic development, create employment and strengthen local production chains. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The RIGI is aimed at investment projects in the forestry industry, tourism, infrastructure, mining, technology, iron and steel, energy and oil and gas
sectors, with a minimum investment per sector or subsector or productive stage equal to or greater than a range between US$ 200,000,000 up to US$&nbsp;900,000,000 in computable assets, as established by the application authority. Interested parties
have 2 years to adhere to the RIGI, submitting and obtaining the approval of an investment plan by the application authority. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The benefits of the
RIGI include a 25% income tax rate, accelerated amortization of investments, <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-expirable</FONT> tax loss carryforwards, indexing tax losses by the Internal Wholesale Price Index (&#147;IPIM&#148;) published by the
INDEC, and exemptions from import and export duties, among others. In addition, foreign exchange incentives are established, such as the free availability of foreign currency on a staggered basis obtained from exports and certain flexibility related
to financing. The RIGI guarantees tax, customs and foreign exchange regulatory stability for 30 years from accession, protecting investment projects from more burdensome legislative changes. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>35.f) Tax regulations </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">During the
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT> period ended June&nbsp;30, 2024, there were no significant updates to the regulatory framework described in Note 35.e) to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>35.g) Custom regulations </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Updates to the regulatory framework
described in Note 35.f) to the annual consolidated financial statements for the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT> period ended June&nbsp;30, 2024, are described below: </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On July&nbsp;1, 2024, AFIP General Resolution No.&nbsp;5,520/2024 was published in the BO, which extend, until December&nbsp;31, 2024, the provisions
established of AFIP General Resolution No.&nbsp;5,339/2023, as amended (see Note 35.f.2) to the annual consolidated financial statements). </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>35.h) Regulations
related to the Foreign Exchange Market </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Updates to the regulatory framework described in Note 35.g) to the annual consolidated financial
statements for the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT> period ended June&nbsp;30, 2024, are described below: </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On April&nbsp;18, 2024,
the BCRA issued Communication &#147;A&#148; 7,994 which allows the possibility of applying the collection of exports to the payment of capital and interest on financial debts abroad that are settled in the Foreign Exchange Market from April&nbsp;19,
2024 and as long as the following conditions are met: (i)&nbsp;the average life of the debt is not less than 3 years; and (ii)&nbsp;the first capital payment is not made before the year it was entered and settled in the Foreign Exchange Market; and
established the possibility of not filing for the BCRA&#146;s prior approval process more than 3 days before the maturity of the capital and interest for access to the Foreign Exchange Market when debt payments abroad are anticipated and as long as
the following conditions are met: (i)&nbsp;the access occurs simultaneously with the settlement of a new financial debt granted by a local financial entity from a line of credit from abroad as of April&nbsp;19, 2024; (ii) the average life of the new
debt is greater than the average remaining life of the anticipated debt; and (ii)&nbsp;the accumulated amount of principal maturities of the new indebtedness does not exceed the accumulated amount of principal maturities of the anticipated debt.
</P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="font-size:90pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:7pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="right">HORACIO DANIEL MAR&Iacute;N </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:7pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="right">President&#8195;&#8195;&#8195;&#8195;&#8195; </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>35. MAIN REGULATIONS (cont.) </B></P> <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On June&nbsp;28, 2024 the BCRA issued Communication &#147;A&#148; 8,055 that established financial
entities may give access to the Foreign Exchange Market for the cancellation in the country or abroad of principal and interest of debt securities denominated in foreign currency, as long as such securities have been fully subscribed abroad and the
funds obtained have been settled in the Foreign Exchange Market. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On July&nbsp;4, 2024 the BCRA issued Communication &#147;A&#148; 8,059 by means of
which the requirement of prior conformity by the BCRA is eliminated to make payments through the Foreign Exchange Market to foreign related counterparties for the following concepts: (i)&nbsp;interests on commercial debts for the import of goods and
services whose maturity date are from July&nbsp;5,2024; (ii) interest on other commercial debts; and (iii)&nbsp;interest on financial indebtedness. In (ii)&nbsp;and (iii) above, access to the Foreign Exchange Market must comply with certain
requirements set forth in the aforementioned Communication. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>35.i) Decree of Necessity and Urgency (&#147;DNU&#148; by its acronym in Spanish) No.&nbsp;70/2023
</B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Updates to the regulatory framework described in Note 35.h) to the annual consolidated financial statements for the <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT> period ended June&nbsp;30, 2024, are described below: </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On March&nbsp;14, 2024, the Chamber of Senators of
the National Congress rejected the Decree No.&nbsp;70/2023, and, as of the date of issuance of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements, is pending to be considered by the Chamber of Deputies of the National Congress. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>35.j) Law of Bases and Starting Points for the Freedom of Argentines No.&nbsp;27,742 (&#147;Bases Law&#148;) </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On July&nbsp;8, 2024, the Bases Law was published in the BO, which introduces several amendments to the Argentine legal framework including, among others:
(i)&nbsp;the declaration of emergency in administrative, economic, financial and energy matters for a term of 1 year; (ii)&nbsp;the administrative reorganization of the National State; (iii)&nbsp;the privatization of certain companies and
corporations wholly or majority owned by the State; (iv)&nbsp;amendments to the Administrative Procedures Law No.&nbsp;19,549; (v) amendments in the energy and oil and gas matters (see Notes 35.a.1) and 35.c.1)); (vi) the creation of the RIGI to
encourage large investments with tax, customs and exchange benefits, guaranteeing legal certainty and the protection of acquired rights (see Note 35.e)); and (vii)&nbsp;a labor and union reform. </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>36. BALANCES AND TRANSACTIONS WITH RELATED PARTIES (cont.) </B></P> <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In addition, the Company performed an external benchmark analysis of the Board of Directors&#146; fees
and compensation of first-line executives. The conclusions were presented to the Compensation and Nomination Committee and, as a result, the components of the total compensation package were aligned with YPF&#146;s strategic plan and market
standards for local and international listed companies of similar magnitude. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As detailed in Note 37, a &#147;Value Generation Plan&#148; applicable
to eligible members of YPF&#146;s Management and a variable compensation based on results (&#147;CVR&#148;) which applies to 100% of the Company&#146;s employees, with the exception of the President and CEO and commercial agents, were implemented.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B><A NAME="item1toc854147_43"></A>37. EMPLOYEE BENEFIT PLANS AND SIMILAR OBLIGATIONS </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Note 37 to the annual consolidated financial statements describes the main characteristics and accounting treatment for employee benefit plans and
similar obligations implemented by the Group. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Retirement plan</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The amount charged to expense related to the Retirement Plan was 2 and 1 for the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT> periods ended
June&nbsp;30, 2024 and 2023, respectively. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Performance bonus programs</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">These programs cover certain of the Group&#146;s personnel and are paid in cash. These bonuses are mainly based on compliance with VPs and related
management objectives. They are calculated considering the annual compensation of each employee and certain key factors related to the fulfillment of these objectives. As of 2024, a new variable bonus program based on corporate results
(&#147;CVR&#148;) was implemented. This will be paid based on the Group&#146;s net profit before income tax, if it is positive. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The amount charged to
expense related to the performance bonus programs was 97 and 60 for the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT> periods ended June&nbsp;30, 2024 and 2023, respectively. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Share-based benefit plans</U> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In April 2024, the
Company adopted the &#147;Value Generation Plan&#148;, which is a long-term remuneration program for eligible members of management of YPF with the objective of incentivizing extraordinary results in the long term and retaining key employees. Under
this Plan, the Company granted 4.6&nbsp;million performance stock appreciation rights (&#147;PSARs&#148;) to plan participants comprising key employees of the Company. The PSARs provide beneficiaries the opportunity to receive an award to be settled
in cash equivalent to the appreciation in the value of the common shares of the Company over a specified period of time. The amount to be paid upon exercise is the difference between the per share base price determined by the plan and the per share
market value of the Company&#146;s common shares as of the exercise date. The PSARs expire five years after their grant and begin to vest in the third year, subject to the fulfillment of certain conditions, including performance milestones related
to the price of the Company&#146;s common shares ranging from a minimum of US$ 30 per common share up to US$ 60 per common share. The beneficiaries of the PSARs are also required to remain in the Company for three years from the granting of the
plan. The PSARs granted by the Company have a base price of US$ 16.17 per share, resulting in a weighted average fair value of US$ 8.75 per PSAR as of the granting date. The Value Generation Plan was approved by the Compensation and Nomination
Committee of the Company with the support of a management consulting firm (Mercer) which advised on its design and implementation. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of
June&nbsp;30, 2024, there are 4.6&nbsp;million number of PSARs outstanding with and a weighted average fair value of US$ 9.03 per PSARs. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">PSARs
expense is determined based on the grant-date fair value of the awards. Fair value is calculated using Monte Carlo simulation model, which requires the input of highly subjective assumptions, including the fair value of the Company&#146;s shares,
expected term and risk-free interest rate. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The amount charged to expense in relation with Value generation Plan was 2, for the <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT> period ended June&nbsp;30, 2024. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The amount charged to expense in relation with the remainder of the
share-based plans was 2 and 1 to be settled in equity instruments, and 9 and 11 to be settled in cash, for the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT> periods ended June&nbsp;30, 2024 and 2023, respectively. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Note 2.b) describes the accounting policies for share-based benefit plans. Repurchases of treasury shares are disclosed in Note 31. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B><A NAME="item1toc854147_44"></A>38. SUBSEQUENT EVENTS </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On July&nbsp;1, 2024 the Company issued Class&nbsp;XXX NO denominated in U.S. dollars, to be integrated in cash and in pesos at the integration exchange
rate and payable in pesos at the applicable exchange rate with maturity in 24 months for an amount of 185 at an issue price of US$ 102 per US$ 100 of nominal value. These NO accrue interest at a fixed annual nominal rate of 1%. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On August&nbsp;5, 2024, assignment agreements have been signed for 6 groups of assets (15 conventional areas), subject to the compliance of closing
conditions including applicable regulatory and provincial approvals. The Company continues to develop the process of assignment or reversal of the remaining assets available for sale as well as compliance with the closing conditions indicated above.
As of the date of issuance of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements and considering the elements of judgment available at such date, the Company expects to comply with the plan within the terms and conditions duly approved by the
Board of Directors of the Company on February&nbsp;29, 2024. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of the date of issuance of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements,
there have been no other significant subsequent events whose effect on the Group&#146;s shareholders&acute; equity, the net comprehensive income or their disclosure in notes to the financial statements for the period ended as of June&nbsp;30, 2024,
should have been considered in such financial statements under IFRS. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">These condensed interim consolidated financial statements were approved by the
Board of Directors&#146; meeting and authorized to be issued on August&nbsp;8, 2024. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The operations, properties and clients of the Group are mainly located in Argentina. However, the Group also holds participating interest in exploratory
areas in Bolivia and sells jet fuel, natural gas, lubricants and derivatives in Chile and lubricants and derivatives in Brazil. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B><A NAME="item2toc854147_8"></A>2. BASIS OF PREPARATION OF THE CONDENSED INTERIM CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>2.a) Applicable accounting framework </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The condensed interim consolidated financial statements of the Company for the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT> period ended
June&nbsp;30, 2024 are presented in accordance with IAS 34 &#147;Interim Financial Reporting&#148;. Therefore, they should be read together with the annual consolidated financial statements of the Company as of December&nbsp;31, 2023 (&#147;annual
consolidated financial statements&#148;) presented in accordance with IFRS as issued by the IASB. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Moreover, some additional information required by
the LGS and/or CNV&#146;s Rules have been included. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">These condensed interim consolidated financial statements corresponding to the <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT> period ended June&nbsp;30, 2024 are unaudited. The Company believes they include all necessary adjustments to reasonably present the results of each period on a basis consistent with the audited annual
consolidated financial statements. Net Income for the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT> period ended June&nbsp;30, 2024 does not necessarily reflect the proportion of the Group&#146;s full-year net income. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>2.b) Material accounting policies </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The material
accounting policies are described in Note 2.b) to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The accounting policies adopted in the preparation of
these condensed interim consolidated financial statements are consistent with those used in the preparation of the annual consolidated financial statements, except for the valuation policy for income tax detailed in Note 18. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Functional and presentation currency</U> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As
mentioned in Note 2.b.1) to the annual consolidated financial statements, YPF has defined the U.S. dollar as its functional currency. Additionally, in accordance with the provisions of the LGS and the CNV Rules, the Company must present its
financial statements in pesos. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Share-based benefit plans</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Group maintains share-based benefit plans with the characteristics mentioned in Note 37 of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements
and Note 37 to the annual consolidated financial statements. Such plans are recorded in accordance with the guidelines set out in IFRS 2 &#147;Share-based Payments&#148;. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify">Equity-settled share-based payment transactions are recognized as a straight-line expense over the period of service,
based on the Group&#146;s estimate of the number of equity instruments that will eventually vest considering their fair value at the grant date, with an offsetting credit entry in the &#147;Share-based benefit plans&#148; account in the statement of
changes in shareholders&#146; equity. At the end of each period, the Group reviews its estimate according to the number of equity instruments it expects will vest based on the grant conditions specified under the respective benefit plan.
