<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Adoption of new standards and interpretations effective as from January&nbsp;1, 2024</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Company has adopted all new and revised standards and interpretations, issued by the IASB, relevant to its operations which are of mandatory and
effective application as of June&nbsp;30, 2024, as described in Note 2.b.14) to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Standards and
interpretations issued by the IASB as of January</U><U></U><U>&nbsp;1, 2024 whose application is not mandatory at the closing date of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements and have not been adopted by the Group</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In accordance with Article 1, Chapter III, Title IV of the CNV Rules, the early application of the IFRS and/or their amendments is not permitted for
issuers filing financial statements with the CNV, unless specifically admitted by such agency. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">&#149;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt"><B>IFRS 18 &#147;Presentation and disclosure in financial statements&#148;</B> </P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In April 2024, the IASB issued IFRS 18, which replaces IAS 1 &#147;Presentation of financial statements&#148;, with the objective of providing better
information on the financial performance of entities, improving their comparability, which is applicable to fiscal years beginning on or after January&nbsp;1, 2027. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">IFRS 18 introduces the following information requirements that can be grouped into 2 main groups: </P>
<P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="3%">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">-</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify">Group income and expenses into 3 defined categories: (i)&nbsp;operating; (ii) financing and (iii)&nbsp;investing, and
include certain defined subtotals, such as the operating result and the result before financing and income tax, with the aim of improving the comparability of the statement of comprehensive income. </P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="3%">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">-</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify">Provide more information about the performance measures defined by management, which, although not mandatory, in the
event of including this type of measures, the entity must disclose the reason why said measures are useful to financial statements users, their method of calculation, a reconciliation between to the most directly comparable subtotal from the
statement of comprehensive income, among others. </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Additionally, IFRS 18 establishes more detailed guidance on how to organize
information within the financial statements and whether it should be provided in the primary financial statements or in the notes, with the aim of improving the grouping of information in the financial statements. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of the date of issuance of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements, the Group is in the process of evaluating the effects of the
application of IFRS 18. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt"><B>IFRS 19 &#147;Subsidiaries without public accountability: Disclosures&#148;</B> </P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In May 2024, the IASB issued IFRS 19 with the objective of allowing the option to apply simplified disclosure requirements in the financial statements of
subsidiaries without public accountability and with a parent company, ultimate or intermediate, that prepares consolidated financial statements for public use in accordance with IFRS. Its application is optional for fiscal years beginning on or
after January&nbsp;1, 2027. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="font-size:80pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="font-size:10pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Historically, the Group&#146;s results have been subject to seasonal fluctuations throughout the year, particularly as a result of the increase in natural
gas sales during the winter driven by the increased demand in the residential segment. Consequently, the Group is subject to seasonal fluctuations in its sales volumes and prices, with higher sales of natural gas during the winter at higher prices.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B><A NAME="item2toc854147_10"></A>4. &#8201;ACQUISITIONS AND DISPOSALS </B></P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B><A NAME="item2toc854147_11"></A>5. &#8201;FINANCIAL RISK MANAGEMENT </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Group&#146;s activities expose it to a variety of financial risks: Market risk (including exchange rate risk, interest rate risk, and price risk),
credit risk and liquidity risk. Within the Group, risk management functions are conducted in relation to financial risks associated to financial instruments to which the Group is exposed during a certain period or as of a specific date. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">During the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT> period ended June&nbsp;30, 2024, there were no significant changes in the administration or
policies of risk management implemented by the Group as described in Note 4 to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE CELLSPACING="0" CELLPADDING="0" WIDTH="100%" BORDER="0" STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:10pt" ALIGN="center">


<TR>

<TD WIDTH="2%"></TD>

<TD VALIGN="bottom" WIDTH="1%"></TD>
<TD WIDTH="97%"></TD></TR>


<TR STYLE="page-break-inside:avoid ; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt">
<TD VALIGN="top"><FONT STYLE="font-size:10pt"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman">&#9679;</FONT></FONT></TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom">&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom"><B>Liquidity risk management</B></TD></TR>
</TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Most of the Group&#146;s loans contain market-standard covenants for contracts of this nature, which include financial
covenants in respect of the Group&#146;s leverage ratio and debt service coverage ratio, and events of defaults triggered by materially adverse judgements, among others. See Notes 16, 32 and 33 to the annual consolidated financial statements and
Notes 17 and 33. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Group monitors compliance with covenants on a quaterly basis. As of June&nbsp;30, 2024, the Group is in compliace with its
covenants. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">It should be noted that, under the terms and conditions of the loans that our subsidiary Metrogas has taken, the interest coverage ratio
would not have been complied with, which could have accelerated the maturities of these financial liabilities. However, the financial creditors formally accepted to waive Metrogas from complying with the contractual obligation related to such
financial ratio, as of June&nbsp;30, 2024. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B><A NAME="item2toc854147_12"></A>6. &#8201;BUSINESS SEGMENT INFORMATION </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The different business segments in which the Group&#146;s organization is structured consider the different activities from which the Group can obtain
revenues and incur expenses. Such organizational structure is based on the way in which the chief decision maker analyzes the main operating and financial magnitudes for making decisions about resource allocation and performance assessment, also
considering the business strategy of the Group. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Business segment information is presented in U.S. dollars, the functional currency of the Company
(see Note 2.b)), consistently with the manner of reporting the information used by the chief decision maker to allocate resources and assess business segment performance. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The business segment structure is organized as follows: </P> <P STYLE="font-size:10pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="2%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="justify" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt"><B>Upstream </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:3%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Upstream business segment performs all activities related to the exploration and exploitation and production of crude oil, natural
gas and frac sand for well drilling/fracking purposes. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:3%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Its revenues are largely derived from: (i)&nbsp;the sale of the crude oil
produced to the Downstream business segment; and (ii)&nbsp;the sale of the natural gas produced and the natural gas retained in plant to the Gas and Power business segment. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:3%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">It incurs all costs related to the activities mentioned above. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:10pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="2%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="justify" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt"><B>Downstream </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:3%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Downstream business segment performs activities related to: (i)&nbsp;crude oil refining and the production of petrochemical products;
(ii)&nbsp;logistics related to the transportation of crude oil to the refineries and the transportation and distribution of refined and petrochemical products to be marketed at the different sales channels; (iii)&nbsp;commercialization of refined
and petrochemical products obtained from such processes; (iv)&nbsp;commercialization of crude oil; and (v)&nbsp;commercialization of specialties for the agribusiness industry and of grains and their
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">by-products.</FONT> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:3%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Its revenues are derived primarily from the sale of crude oil, refined and
petrochemical products, specialties for the agribusiness industry and grains and their <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">by-products.</FONT> These operations are performed through the businesses of B2C (Retail), B2B (Industries, Transportation,

investments in associates and joint ventures, the Gas and Power business segment undertakes activities related to: (i)&nbsp;separation of natural gas liquids and their fractionation, storage and transportation for the production of ethane, propane,
butane and natural gasoline; (ii)&nbsp;generation of conventional thermal electric power and renewable energy; and (iii)&nbsp;production, storage, distribution and sale of fertilizers. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:3%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Its revenues are largely derived from the commercialization of natural gas as producers to third parties and the Downstream business
segment, the distribution of natural gas through our subsidiary Metrogas, the sale of natural gasoline, propane and butane to the Downstream business segment and the provision of LNG regasification services. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Group capitalizes the financial cost of loans as part of the cost of the property, plant and
equipment. For the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT> periods ended June&nbsp;30, 2024 and 2023, the rate of capitalization was 7.66% and 8.13%, respectively, and the amount capitalized amounted to 3,083 and 2,089, respectively. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Set forth below is the evolution of the provision for obsolescence of materials and equipment for the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT>
period ended June&nbsp;30, 2024 and as of the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2023: </P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B><A NAME="item2toc854147_24"></A>18. INCOME TAX </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">According to IAS 34, income tax expense is recognized in each interim period based on the best estimate of the effective income tax rate expected as of
the closing date of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements, considering the tax criteria that the Group assumes to apply during the fiscal year. If the estimate of such rate is modified based on new elements of judgment, the
income tax expense could require adjustments in subsequent periods. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In relation to such tax criteria, the income tax expense contemplates the
application of the integral inflation adjustment mechanism applicable to property, plant and equipment, and the indexation of the accumulated tax losses carryforward until the concurrence of the projected tax result of the fiscal year 2024, all
considering that the assumption of confiscation would be verified in accordance with the jurisprudence of the CSJN in force as of the date of issuance of these consolidated financial statements. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Company considers having strong arguments to successfully defend such assumed tax criteria, in the event of a possible controversy with the tax
authorities, in accordance with the guidelines of IFRIC 23 &#147;Uncertainty over income tax treatments&#148;. As of June&nbsp;30, 2024, the assumed tax criteria generates a profit of 289,917. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The income tax charge for the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT> period ending June&nbsp;30, 2024 is a profit of 172,891. The amount
accrued for the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-periods</FONT> ending June&nbsp;30, 2024 and 2023 is as follows: </P> <P STYLE="font-size:10pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B><A NAME="item2toc854147_37"></A>31. SHAREHOLDERS&#146; EQUITY </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of June&nbsp;30, 2024, the Company&#146;s capital amounts to 3,919 and treasury shares amount to 14 represented by 393,312,793 book-entry shares of
common stock and divided into four classes of shares (A, B, C and D), with a par value of 10 pesos and 1 vote per share. These shares are fully subscribed, <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">paid-in</FONT> and authorized for stock exchange listing.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of June&nbsp;30, 2024, there are 3,764 Class&nbsp;A outstanding shares. As long as any Class&nbsp;A share remains outstanding, the affirmative
vote of the Argentine Government is required for: (i)&nbsp;mergers; (ii) acquisitions of more than 50% of YPF shares in an agreed or hostile bid; (iii)&nbsp;transfers of all the YPF&#146;s production and exploration rights; (iv)&nbsp;the voluntary
dissolution of YPF; (v)&nbsp;change of corporate and/or tax address outside Argentina; or (vi)&nbsp;make an acquisition that would result in the purchaser holding 15% or more of the Company&#146;s capital stock, or 20% or more of the outstanding
Class&nbsp;D shares. Items (iii)&nbsp;and (iv) also require prior approval by the Argentine Congress. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On April&nbsp;26, 2024, the General
Shareholders&#146; Meeting was held, which approved the statutory financial statements of YPF corresponding to the year ended on December&nbsp;31, 2023 and, additionally, approved the following in relation to the retained earnings:
(i)&nbsp;completely disaffect the reserve for future dividends, the reserve for purchase of treasury shares and the reserve for investments; (ii)&nbsp;absorb accumulated losses in unappropriated retained earnings and losses up to the amount of
1,003,419; (iii) allocate the amount of 28,745 to constitute a reserve for purchase of treasury shares; and (iv)&nbsp;allocate the amount of 3,418,972 to constitute a reserve for investments. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">During the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT> periods ended June&nbsp;30, 2024 and 2023, the Company has not repurchased any of its own
shares. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B><A NAME="item2toc854147_38"></A>32. EARNINGS PER SHARE </B></P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On April&nbsp;1, 2024, Plaintiffs filed a turnover motion, which became public (and accessible to YPF) on April&nbsp;22, 2024. This motion requests that
the District Court order the Republic to turn over the YPF Class&nbsp;D shares held by the Republic to Plaintiffs in partial satisfaction of the District Court&#146;s judgment against the Republic in this proceeding. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Plaintiffs and the Republic completed their briefing on the turnover motion on July&nbsp;8, 2024. The District Court may, but is not required to, hold
oral argument prior to rendering a decision on the turnover motion. Furthermore, the District Court&#146;s decision on the turnover motion may be appealed by Plaintiffs or the Republic in accordance with applicable procedural rules. YPF is not a
party to the turnover motion. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Plaintiffs are also seeking discovery of documents from YPF related to their theory that YPF could be an &#147;alter
ego&#148; of the Republic. YPF denies that it is an <I>alter ego</I> and objected to Plaintiffs&#146; document requests. On May&nbsp;28, 2024, the District Court ordered YPF to produce documents in response to Plaintiffs&#146; discovery requests. To
date, Plaintiffs have not requested that the District Court find that YPF is an <I>alter ego</I> of the Republic, and the District Court&#146;s order on discovery is not a ruling accepting Plaintiffs&#146; <I>alter ego</I> theory. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">YPF will continue to defend itself in accordance with the applicable legal procedures and available defenses. </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>35.a) Regulations applicable to the hydrocarbon industry </B></P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Through the Bases Law (see Note 35.j)), amendments were incorporated in relation to the Hydrocarbons Law, as described below: </P>
<P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

export hydrocarbons and/or their derivatives, subject to the SE&#146;s <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-objection.</FONT> The effective exercise of this right will be subject to regulations issued by the PEN, which, among other aspects, must
consider: (i)&nbsp;the usual requirements related to the access to technically proven resources; and (ii)&nbsp;that the eventual objection of the SE may only be formulated within 30 days of being informed of the exports to be made, and must be based

<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">-</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify">Determines that in exploitation concession bidding processes the royalties to be paid to the application authority will
be offered by the concessionaire, determining that the royalty to be offered will be 15% plus or minus a percentage to be chosen by the bidder. </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<TD WIDTH="4%">&nbsp;</TD>

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify">Other modifications establish that: (i)&nbsp;the request for conversion of a conventional exploitation concession into
a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-conventional</FONT> exploitation concession will only be available until December&nbsp;31, 2028 and its term will be 35 years without extensions; (ii)&nbsp;for new exploitation concessions, the national or
provincial Executive Branch, as applicable, at the time of defining the terms and conditions of the bidding, may determine in a reasoned manner other terms of up to 10 years more than those provided for in the Hydrocarbons Law; (iii)&nbsp;owners of
projects and/or facilities for the conditioning, separation, fractionation, liquefaction and/or any other hydrocarbon industrialization process may request an authorization to transport hydrocarbons and/or their derivatives to their
industrialization facilities and from the same to subsequent industrialization or commercialization process centers and/or facilities; (iv)&nbsp;those authorized to process hydrocarbons must process hydrocarbons from third parties up to a maximum of
5% of the capacity of their facilities; and (v)&nbsp;the fee for each square kilometer or fraction thereof that a holder of an exploration permit must pay annually and in advance shall be calculated according to a scale determined by the price of a
barrel of oil quoted on the &#147;Frontline ICE Brent&#148;. </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>35.b) Regulations applicable to the Downstream segment </B></P>

<p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On 5&nbsp;June 2024, SE Resolution No.&nbsp;93/2024 was published in the BO, which approved natural gas

<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>35.e) Investment incentive programs </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Large
Investment Incentive Regime (&#147;RIGI&#148;)</U> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Bases Law (see Note 35.j)) created the RIGI, intended to encourage large investments with tax,
customs and exchange benefits, guaranteeing legal certainty and the protection of acquired rights. This regime seeks to encourage investments, promote economic development, create employment and strengthen local production chains. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The RIGI is aimed at investment projects in the forestry industry, tourism, infrastructure, mining, technology, iron and steel, energy and oil and gas
sectors, with a minimum investment per sector or subsector or productive stage equal to or greater than a range between US$ 200,000,000 up to US$ 900,000,000 in computable assets, as established by the application authority. Interested parties have
2 years to adhere to the RIGI, submitting and obtaining the approval of an investment plan by the application authority. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The benefits of the RIGI
include a 25% income tax rate, accelerated amortization of investments, <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-expirable</FONT> tax loss carryforwards, indexing tax losses by the Internal Wholesale Price Index (&#147;IPIM&#148;) published by the
INDEC, and exemptions from import and export duties, among others. In addition, foreign exchange incentives are established, such as the free availability of foreign currency on a staggered basis obtained from exports and certain flexibility related
to financing. The RIGI guarantees tax, customs and foreign exchange regulatory stability for 30 years from accession, protecting investment projects from more burdensome legislative changes. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>35.f) Tax regulations </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">During the <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT> period ended June&nbsp;30, 2024, there were no significant updates to the regulatory framework described in Note 35.e) to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>35.g) Custom regulations </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Updates to the regulatory framework
described in Note 35.f) to the annual consolidated financial statements for the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT> period ended June&nbsp;30, 2024, are described below: </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On July&nbsp;1, 2024, AFIP General Resolution No.&nbsp;5,520/2024 was published in the BO, which extend, until December&nbsp;31, 2024, the provisions
established of AFIP General Resolution No.&nbsp;5,339/2023, as amended (see Note 35.f.2) to the annual consolidated financial statements). </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>35.h) Regulations
related to the Foreign Exchange Market </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Updates to the regulatory framework described in Note 35.g) to the annual consolidated financial
statements for the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT> period ended June&nbsp;30, 2024, are described below: </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On April&nbsp;18, 2024,
the BCRA issued Communication &#147;A&#148; 7,994 which allows the possibility of applying the collection of exports to the payment of capital and interest on financial debts abroad that are settled in the Foreign Exchange Market from April&nbsp;19,
2024 and as long as the following conditions are met: (i)&nbsp;the average life of the debt is not less than 3 years; and (ii)&nbsp;the first capital payment is not made before the year it was entered and settled in the Foreign Exchange Market; and
established the possibility of not filing for the BCRA&#146;s prior approval process more than 3 days before the maturity of the capital and interest for access to the Foreign Exchange Market when debt payments abroad are anticipated and as long as
the following conditions are met: (i)&nbsp;the access occurs simultaneously with the settlement of a new financial debt granted by a local financial entity from a line of credit from abroad as of April&nbsp;19, 2024; (ii) the average life of the new
debt is greater than the average remaining life of the anticipated debt; and (ii)&nbsp;the accumulated amount of principal maturities of the new indebtedness does not exceed the accumulated amount of principal maturities of the anticipated debt.

<p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On June&nbsp;28, 2024 the BCRA issued Communication &#147;A&#148; 8,055 that established financial
entities may give access to the Foreign Exchange Market for the cancellation in the country or abroad of principal and interest of debt securities denominated in foreign currency, as long as such securities have been fully subscribed abroad and the
funds obtained have been settled in the Foreign Exchange Market. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On July&nbsp;4, 2024 the BCRA issued Communication &#147;A&#148; 8,059 by means of
which the requirement of prior conformity by the BCRA is eliminated to make payments through the Foreign Exchange Market to foreign related counterparties for the following concepts: (i)&nbsp;interests on commercial debts for the import of goods and
services whose maturity date are from July&nbsp;5,2024; (ii) interest on other commercial debts; and (iii)&nbsp;interest on financial indebtedness. In (ii)&nbsp;and (iii) above, access to the Foreign Exchange Market must comply with certain
requirements set forth in the aforementioned Communication. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>35.i) Decree of Necessity and Urgency (&#147;DNU&#148; by its acronym in Spanish)
No.&nbsp;70/2023 </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Updates to the regulatory framework described in Note 35.h) to the annual consolidated financial statements for the <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT> period ended June&nbsp;30, 2024, are described below: </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On March&nbsp;14, 2024, the Chamber of Senators of
the National Congress rejected the Decree No.&nbsp;70/2023, and, as of the date of issuance of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements, is pending to be considered by the Chamber of Deputies of the National Congress. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>35.j) Law of Bases and Starting Points for the Freedom of Argentines No.&nbsp;27,742 (&#147;Bases Law&#148;) </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On July&nbsp;8, 2024, the Bases Law was published in the BO, which introduces several amendments to the Argentine legal framework including, among others:
(i)&nbsp;the declaration of emergency in administrative, economic, financial and energy matters for a term of 1 year; (ii)&nbsp;the administrative reorganization of the National State; (iii)&nbsp;the privatization of certain companies and
corporations wholly or majority owned by the State; (iv)&nbsp;amendments to the Administrative Procedures Law No.&nbsp;19,549; (v) amendments in the energy and oil and gas matters (see Notes 35.a.1) and 35.c.1)); (vi) the creation of the RIGI to
encourage large investments with tax, customs and exchange benefits, guaranteeing legal certainty and the protection of acquired rights (see Note 35.e)); and (vii)&nbsp;a labor and union reform. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>35.k) CNV regulatory framework </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Information
requirements as Settlement and Clearing Agent and Trading Agent</U> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of the date of issuance of these condensed interim consolidated financial
statements, the Company is registered in the CNV under the category &#147;Settlement and Clearing Agent and Trading Agent - Direct Participant&#148;, record No.&nbsp;549. Considering the Company&#146;s business and the CNV Rules, the Company will
not, under any circumstance, offer brokerage services to third parties for transactions in markets under the jurisdiction of the CNV, and it will also not open operating accounts to third parties to issue orders and trade in markets under the
jurisdiction of the CNV. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In accordance with the CNV Rules, the Company is subject to the provisions of Article 5 c), Chapter II, Title VII of the CNV
Rules, &#147;Settlement and Clearing Agent - Direct Participant&#148;. In this respect, as set forth in Article 13, Chapter II, Title VII, of the CNV Rules, as of June&nbsp;30, 2024, the equity of the Company exceeds the minimum equity required by
such Rules, which amounts to 490. </P>

<p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Additionally, the Group has entered into certain financing and insurance transactions with entities
related to the national public sector. Such transactions consist of certain financial transactions that are described in Notes 15, 16 and 22 and transactions with Naci&oacute;n Seguros S.A. related to certain insurance policies contracts. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On the other hand, the Group holds Bonds of the Argentine Republic 2029, 2030 and 2038, and BCRA bonds identified as investments in financial assets at
fair value through profit or loss, and bills and bonds issued by the National Government and BCRA bonds identified as investments in financial assets at amortized cost (see Note 15). Additionally, the Group holds BCRA bills identified as cash and
cash equivalents (see Note 16). </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Furthermore, YPF has an indirect <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-controlling</FONT> interest in
Compa&ntilde;&iacute;a de Hidrocarburo No Convencional S.R.L. (&#147;CHNC&#148;). During the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT> periods ended June&nbsp;30, 2024 and 2023, YPF and CHNC carried out transactions, among others, the
purchases of crude oil by YPF for 206,660 and 53,137, respectively. These transactions were consummated in accordance with the general and regulatory conditions of the market. The net balance payable to CHNC as of June&nbsp;30, 2024 and
December&nbsp;31, 2023 amounts to 58,175 and 31,003, respectively. See Note 36 to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On May&nbsp;8, 2024,
SE Resolution No.&nbsp;58/2024 was published in the BO, which establishes an exceptional, transitory and unique payment regime for the balance of the MEM&#146;s economic transactions of December 2023, January 2024 and February 2024 corresponding to
the MEM&#146;s creditors, and instructs CAMMESA to determine the amounts owed to each of them corresponding to such economic transactions, to be cancelled as follows: (i)&nbsp;the economic transactions of December 2023 and January 2024, through the
delivery of government securities denominated &#147;Bonos de la Rep&uacute;blica Argentina en D&oacute;lares Estadounidenses Step Up 2038&#148;; and (ii)&nbsp;the economic transactions of February 2024, with the funds available in the bank accounts
enabled in CAMMESA for collection purposes and with those funds available from the transfers made by the National Goverment to the &#147;Fondo Unificado con Destino al Fondo de Estabilizaci&oacute;n&#148;. </P>

<p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In addition, the Company performed an external benchmark analysis of the Board of Directors&#146; fees

</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B><A NAME="item2toc854147_43"></A>37. EMPLOYEE BENEFIT PLANS AND SIMILAR OBLIGATIONS </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Note 37 to the annual consolidated financial statements describes the main characteristics and accounting treatment for employee benefit plans and similar
obligations implemented by the Group. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Retirement plan</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The amount charged to expense related to the Retirement Plan was 1,680 and 395 for the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT> periods ended
June&nbsp;30, 2024 and 2023, respectively. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Performance bonus programs</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">These programs cover certain of the Group&#146;s personnel and are paid in cash. These bonuses are mainly based on compliance with VPs and related
management objectives. They are calculated considering the annual compensation of each employee and certain key factors related to the fulfillment of these objectives. As of 2024, a new variable bonus program based on corporate results
(&#147;CVR&#148;) was implemented. This will be paid based on the Group&#146;s net profit before income tax, if it is positive. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The amount charged to
expense related to the performance bonus programs was 86,072 and 13,417 for the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT> periods ended June&nbsp;30, 2024 and 2023, respectively. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Share-based benefit plans</U> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In April 2024, the
Company adopted the &#147;Value Generation Plan&#148;, which is a long-term remuneration program for eligible members of management of YPF with the objective of incentivizing extraordinary results in the long term and retaining key employees. Under
this Plan, the Company granted 4.6&nbsp;million performance stock appreciation rights (&#147;PSARs&#148;) to plan participants comprising key employees of the Company. The PSARs provide beneficiaries the opportunity to receive an award to be settled
in cash equivalent to the appreciation in the value of the common shares of the Company over a specified period of time. The amount to be paid upon exercise is the difference between the per share base price determined by the plan and the per share
market value of the Company&#146;s common shares as of the exercise date. The PSARs expire five years after their grant and begin to vest in the third year, subject to the fulfillment of certain conditions, including performance milestones related
to the price of the Company&#146;s common shares ranging from a minimum of US$ 30 per common share up to US$ 60 per common share. The beneficiaries of the PSARs are also required to remain in the Company for three years from the granting of the
plan. The PSARs granted by the Company have a base price of US$ 16.17 per share, resulting in a weighted average fair value of US$ 8.75 per PSAR as of the granting date. The Value Generation Plan was approved by the Compensation and Nomination
Committee of the Company with the support of a management consulting firm (Mercer) which advised on its design and implementation. </P>

</TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>37. EMPLOYEE BENEFIT PLANS AND SIMILAR OBLIGATIONS (cont.) </B></P>
<p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of June&nbsp;30, 2024, there are 4.6&nbsp;million number of PSARs outstanding with and a weighted
average fair value of US$ 9.03 per PSARs. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">PSARs expense is determined based on the grant-date fair value of the awards. Fair value is calculated
using Monte Carlo simulation model, which requires the input of highly subjective assumptions, including the fair value of the Company&#146;s shares, expected term and risk-free interest rate. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The amount charged to expense in relation with Value generation Plan was 2,162 for the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT> period ended
June&nbsp;30, 2024. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The amount charged to expense in relation with the remainder of the share-based plans was 1,986 and 238 to be settled in equity
instruments, and 8,265 and 2,299 to be settled in cash, for the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT> periods ended June&nbsp;30, 2024 and 2023, respectively. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Note 2.b) describes the accounting policies for share-based benefit plans. Repurchases of treasury shares are disclosed in Note 31. </P>
